Ossification :- Ossification is defined as process of formation of bone starting from cartilage or connective tissue to fully developed bone.

Type of Ossification :-
Intramembranous Ossification.
Endochondral Ossification.

Endochondral Ossification :- In Endochondral Ossification bone is developed from cartilage which is replaced by bone after a period of time. In endochondral Ossification cartilage model is necessary. the endochondral Ossification is developed in bone which is categorized by bone of double bone.

--- Page 3 ---
Interchondral Ossification is seen in Pelvis & long bone

Bones of Endochondral Ossification:

Endochondral Ossification starts from cartilage or connective tissue at 8th week further before become a bone in cartilage then induces a line which is used for the determination of the individual becoming the cartilage bone then after surfaced by bone specially in cartilage Endochondral Ossification in cartilage bone

Ex Pelvis, long bone in cartilage bone

It also occur in Membranous & cartilage bone (Combination)

Note:
Skull: Skull is the bony structure that protects the cranial cavity of the head. It helps in formation of structure composed of 22 bones. Skull is used for identification like Age, sex race etc.

Male Skull is generally robust, large & more prominent than female skull.

Detail Description of Male skull:-
1) General Appearance: Male skull is larger, heavier & more massive in nature.
2) Architecture: Architecture of Male skull is rugged or rough.

--- Page 5 ---
3) Cranial capacity: Cranial capacity of Male skull is 1400 - 1550 ml.

4) Digastric groove: Digastric groove of Male skull is deep whereas Female skull have shallow.

5) Parietal & frontal eminences: Parietal & Frontal Eminences of Male skull is less prominent which is less prominent in Male skull this is only characteristic

6) Mastoid process: large

7) Occipital protuberance: Occipital protuberance [at back] of male skull is more prominent.

8) Antramasal Angulation: At is angulated in male whereas

--- Page 6 ---
9) condylar facet: straight in female
condylar facet is large
10) Palatine: palatine of male skull is u-shaped
11) Zygomatic arch: Zygomatic arch (cheek bone) is more prominent in male skull
12) forehead: forehead of male skull is sloping whereas female has vertical
13) Orbit: Orbit of male skull is rounded margin & square
14) Foramen Magnum:
15) Nasal Aperture: it is long in nature
16) chin: Wide
17) Lips: U-shaped large

--- Page 8 ---
* Measuring process - (for measurement we use landmark):
1) Head -
Head length :- [G-of] we measure from glabella [Medial point of sagittal] to opisthocranion [back of skull]
Head circumference :- [G-of-g] we measure from glabella to opisthocranion then again glabella for finding overall measurement of head
Head breadth :- [eu-eu] we measure from leften [the lateral side of forehead] to righten [the other side] left to right or vice versa

2) Face -
Face measure is generally divided into 2 type
Morphological :- [En-fn]

--- Page 9 ---
We measure from nasion [ Mid-point b/w eyes ] to gnathion [ at chin lower point ]
Physiological : [ t - gn ]
We measure from tryion [ the uppermost point of head ] to gnathion.

3) Nose height - Nose 1-
Nose height 1- (sn - pn)
We measure from sub nasale to pro-nasale
(sn of nose - tip of nose)

- Nose length 1- (sn - pn)
nasion to pro nasale

- Nose breadth 1- al to al
Measure from alare [ the corner of nose ] to alare

4) Height 1-
Standing Height 1-
Measure from Vertex to floor which
individual is in arm-hanging position with eye-ear
(uppermost point)
(uppermost head)

Mana:
Sitting height: from vertex to floor but with straight back with eye - Ear plane.

Somatometry: Somatometry is defined as measurement of various parts of body generally used for identification of especially person identification. Done by instruments: Anthropometric rod, sliding caliper, etc.

Different Somatometric measurements:
Head:
Head length [G-op]: Head length from glabella [the medial point of Sagittal plane] to opistocranion [the back of skull].
Head circumference [G-op-G]: We measure head circumference from glabella to opistocranion and then again till glabella (i.e. in single plane for finding overall measurement of head.
Head Breadth [Eu-Eu]

--- Page 26 ---
2) Head-
Face-
face measurement is divided into two types
Non Physiological [gn] height
We measure the face length from nasion (top of nose) to gnathion (a lower point of chin)
Physiological [t gn]
We measure the face height from t to gnathion

3) Nose-
Nose Height [sn-pn]
We measure the nose height from [base of nose] to pro nasion [tip of nose]

--- Page 27 ---
- Nose length [cm/in]
We measure the nose length from nasion [root of nose] to pronasion [base of nose]
- Nose breadth [cm/all]
We measure the nose breadth from alare [the corner of nose] to nose columella.
- Height-
Standing Height: Measure from vertex [the utmost point of head] to floor when the individual is standing in arm hanging position with eye-ear plane.
Sitting height: from vertex to floor but with straight back & eye-ear plane.
- Body weight: Measure from weighing machine [standing on weighing machine] with minimum clothes of bare foot

--- Page 28 ---
* Importance of somatometry in forensic examinations across diverse populations:

1) Somatometry is used for human identifications:
We can determine age, height, sex, weight by measurement of human body.

2) Archaeology:
We can determine old bodies by measurements of body.

3) Mass disaster cases:
We can use it in forensic identification of mass disaster cases when the body is burned, decomposed etc.

4) Uniqueness:
Every individual have unique characteristics which can be used for identifications.
